ImpersonationToken.description:
The success case of IssueImpersonationTokenResult: a signed, short-lived bearer token
and the identity it acts as. The string ImpersonationToken.Token is a credential: it is deliberately absent from
string ImpersonationToken.ToString() and the debugger display so it cannot leak through an incidental log line.

actorId.description: The real caller the token was issued to, recorded in its `act` claim.

expiresAt.description: When the token stops being valid (UTC).

roles.description: The effective roles: the token's `role` claims.

token.description: The compact serialized token to present as `Authorization: Bearer ...`.

tokenType.description: The scheme to present string ImpersonationToken.Token under; always `Bearer`.

IssueImpersonationTokenRequest.description:
Request body for Task<IActionResult> ImpersonationController.IssueTokenAsync(IssueImpersonationTokenRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default(CancellationToken)). Every member is
nullable here so a missing one is reported by the application's validator as a per-field 400, like
every other rule, rather than by model binding.

examples.reason: Reproducing the checkout error alice reported

lifetimeMinutes.description: The requested lifetime; defaults to the configured default and may not exceed the configured maximum.

reason.description: Why the impersonation is needed, 10 to 500 characters. Required; recorded in the token and the audit trail.

roles.description: The roles to grant. Each must be assignable, and a non-administrator may grant only roles they hold. Optional.

targetUserId.description: The identity the token acts as (its `sub`). Required; not the caller's own id.

ticketReference.description: An optional ticket or case reference, up to 100 characters.

PagedResultOfProductDto.description: A single page of T, plus enough metadata for a caller to compute whether further pages exist.

firstPage.description:
The number of the first page.
Always 1; pages are 1-based.

items.description:
The rows for this page only — never the full result set.
The non-null page rows.

lastPage.description:
The number of the last page at the current int PagedResult<T>.PageSize.
int PagedResult<T>.TotalPages, but never less than 1: a result with no rows still has one (empty) page.

nextPage.description:
The next page's number.
`null` when int PagedResult<T>.PageNumber is the last page or beyond it.

pageNumber.description: The 1-based page number this result represents.

pageSize.description: The page size that was requested, not necessarily IReadOnlyList<T> PagedResult<T>.Items's count (the last page is typically shorter).

previousPage.description:
The previous page's number.
`null` on the first page. From a page past the end, the real int PagedResult<T>.LastPage, so a client can always navigate back to data.

sort.description: The sort keys that were applied, in priority order (the implicit trailing ProductId Product.Id tiebreaker is not listed).

totalCount.description: The total number of rows across all pages, used to compute int PagedResult<T>.TotalPages.

totalPages.description:
The total number of pages, rounded up — e.g. 10 total rows at a page size of 3 yields 4 pages, the last with only 1 row.
The page count implied by int PagedResult<T>.TotalCount and int PagedResult<T>.PageSize; never negative, but callers must guard against a zero int PagedResult<T>.PageSize.

PatchProductRequest.description:
A JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396, `application/merge-patch+json`) for a product. Each member is
either absent (leave that field alone) or present (replace it). A member present as `null`
is rejected — name and price are required, so there is nothing to clear — as is a body that names
neither. Members this contract does not know are ignored, as RFC 7396 leaves unrecognised members
to the recipient. Binding the Optional<T> members is the job of
`OptionalJsonConverterFactory`; every rule on their values belongs to the application's
validator.

name.description: The new display name, when present.

ProductDto.description: The read shape of a product returned across every "success" case in this feature's unions.

createdAt.description: The instant the product was created (UTC).

version.description: The product's concurrency version; the API renders it as the `ETag` a client echoes back in `If-Match`.

ProductId.description:
A Guid-backed identity for Product. Generated by Vogen from the
`[ValueObject]` attribute — <see cref="M:MediatrUnionPoc.Domain.ProductId.Validate(System.Guid)" /> is called from every generated
factory (`From`, `TryFrom`) so an empty guid can never enter the system, and
equality/hashing/string ProductId.ToString() are all structural rather than reference-based.
Serializes as a bare GUID string (see Conversions.SystemTextJson), not as an
object — the Infrastructure layer's `ProductIdValueConverter` handles the equivalent
round-trip through EF Core instead.

ProductSort.description: One key of a multi-key sort: a ProductSortField and the SortDirection to order it in.

ProductSortField.description:
The allowlist of Product properties a listing may be sorted by. An enum rather
than a property-name string, so a caller can never name anything outside this set. Serialized
as the camel-case name the HTTP `sort` parameter uses.

ProductVersion.description:
The optimistic-concurrency version of a Product: a positive long
that starts at 1 for a new product and is advanced by the domain (never by the database) on
every mutation. Two writers that both loaded version `n` cannot both win — whoever writes
second finds the stored version is no longer `n`.

SortDirection.description: Which way a sort key orders its rows. Serialized as its lower-case name.

UpdateProductRequest.description: Request body for Task<IActionResult> ProductsController.UpdateAsync(Guid id, UpdateProductRequest request, string? ifMatchHeader, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default(CancellationToken)).

Bearer.description: A JWT signed with the configured key. The sub claim identifies the caller (and becomes a product's owner); a role claim of Administrator allows deletes.

requestBody.description: Who to act as, which roles to grant, why, and for how long.

post.summary:
Creates a product. The authenticated caller becomes its owner: the value of their
string ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier claim (the token's `sub`) is recorded as
string Product.OwnerId, which is what later updates are checked against. A caller
whose token has no `sub` is authenticated but has no identity to own anything with, so the
request is refused with a NotAuthorized outcome (403) before anything is sent.
